amphicoelous.definition: Describes a vertebra whose main body is hollow at both the front and the back.
amphicoelous.etymology: Greek amphi, "on both sides", and koilos, "hollow".

anterior.definition: Toward the front of the animal, the end with the head. The opposite of posterior.

articulated.definition: Of bones: found still joined together as they were in life. Disarticulated bones were found separated from each other.

associated-skeleton.definition: Bones found together and thought to come from a single animal, though not joined as they were in life.

autapomorphy.definition: A feature found in only one species or genus, which sets it apart from all its relatives. Autapomorphies show that a name represents a distinct animal.
autapomorphy.etymology: Greek autos, "self", apo, "away from", and morphe, "form".

bonebed.definition: A layer of rock packed with the bones of many animals, often buried together.

caudal-vertebra.definition: A vertebra of the tail. Caudal means "of the tail" or "toward the tail".

centrum.definition: The spool-shaped main body of a vertebra, which bears the weight. The spinal cord runs along its top, inside the neural arch.

cervical-vertebra.definition: A vertebra of the neck. Cervical means "of the neck".

character.definition: In a phylogenetic analysis, a feature that differs among the animals studied, such as the shape of a bone, recorded for each animal to work out how they are related.

chevron.definition: A small bone that hangs below the joint between two tail vertebrae, protecting blood vessels and anchoring tail muscles.
chevron.etymology: French, a V-shaped stripe, after its shape.

chimera.definition: A specimen, or a name based on one, made up of bones that turned out to come from more than one kind of animal.
chimera.etymology: The Chimera of Greek myth, a monster made of parts of several animals.

clade.definition: A group made up of an ancestor and all of its descendants. Every branch of a family tree is a clade.

combined-directions.definition: Words that join two directions. Anteroposterior means "from front to back", so a bone that is anteroposteriorly long is long from front to back; anterodorsal means "toward the front and the top".

consensus-tree.definition: A family tree that combines several equally good trees from one analysis, keeping only the groupings they all agree on.

convergence.definition: The evolution of similar features in animals that aren't closely related, often because they lived in similar ways.

cursorial.definition: Built for running, with long, slender legs.

dental-battery.definition: Rows of tightly packed teeth that worked together as one grinding or slicing surface, with new teeth constantly growing in to replace worn ones, as in hadrosaurs and ceratopsids.

derived.definition: Describes a member of a group that branched off later in the group's family tree, or a feature that changed from the ancestral condition. The opposite of early-diverging.

distal.definition: Farther from the body, or from where a limb or bone attaches. The knee end of the thighbone is its distal end. On a tooth, distal means "toward the back of the jaw".

dorsal.definition: Toward the back or top of the animal, the side the backbone runs along. The opposite of ventral. Dorsal also names the vertebrae of the back.

dorsal-vertebra.definition: A vertebra of the back, between the neck and the hips. Most carry ribs.

early-diverging.definition: Describes a member of a group that branched off early in the group's family tree, near its base. It need not be older or simpler than its relatives. Also called basal.

family.definition: A rank in traditional classification that groups related genera. Family names end in -idae, as in Tyrannosauridae.

fragmentary.definition: Of a fossil: known only from broken or incomplete pieces.

gondwana.definition: The southern supercontinent made up of today's South America, Africa, Madagascar, India, Antarctica and Australia, which broke apart during the age of dinosaurs.
gondwana.etymology: From a region of India, "forest of the Gonds".

grade.definition: A set of animals at a similar stage of evolution that don't form a single clade, such as the early sauropodomorphs once grouped together as prosauropods.

holotype.definition: The single specimen a species' name is tied to, chosen when the species is named. Other fossils are compared with it to decide whether they belong to the same species.

incertae-sedis.definition: Used for an animal that belongs to a larger group when where it fits within that group can't be decided.

isolated.definition: Of a fossil: found on its own, apart from any skeleton, as with an isolated tooth. An isolated bone is hard to assign to a species.

juvenile.definition: A young animal, not yet fully grown. A subadult was nearly grown.

labial.definition: On the side of a tooth or jaw that faces the lips or cheek, outside the mouth. The opposite of lingual.

lateral.definition: Toward the side of the animal, away from the line that runs down the middle of its body. The opposite of medial.

laurasia.definition: The northern supercontinent made up of today's North America, Europe and most of Asia, which broke apart during the age of dinosaurs.

least-inclusive-clade.definition: The smallest clade that contains all the named animals. Defining a clade this way picks out the last common ancestor of those animals and all its descendants.

lectotype.definition: A specimen chosen after a species was named, from among its syntypes, to be the single specimen its name is tied to.

lineage.definition: A line of descent: an ancestor and the descendants that follow from it over time.

lingual.definition: On the side of a tooth or jaw that faces the tongue, inside the mouth. The opposite of labial.

manus.definition: The hand. Manual means "of the hand".

medial.definition: Toward the line that runs down the middle of the animal's body. The opposite of lateral.

mesial.definition: On a tooth, the side toward the front of the jaw, following the curve of the tooth row. The opposite of distal.

monophyletic.definition: Describes a group that includes an ancestor and all of its descendants. A monophyletic group is a clade.

monotypic.definition: Containing only one member: a monotypic genus has a single species.

neotype.definition: A specimen chosen to replace a holotype that has been lost or destroyed, or that can no longer be identified, so the name has a specimen to rest on again.

neural-arch.definition: The arch of bone on top of a vertebra's main body, which encloses the spinal cord. The neural spine and most of the vertebra's other projections grow from it.

neural-spine.definition: The blade or rod of bone that sticks up from the top of a vertebra, where back muscles and ligaments attach. Very tall neural spines formed sails or humps in some dinosaurs.

nomen-dubium.definition: A name based on fossils that can't be reliably told apart from those of related animals, so it may not represent a distinct species or genus.

nomen-nudum.definition: A name published without the description or other details the naming rules require, so it isn't a valid name.

ontogeny.definition: The growth and development of an animal from hatching to adulthood. Ontogenetic changes can make young and old animals of one species look like different species.

opisthocoelous.definition: Describes a vertebra whose main body is rounded at the front and hollow at the back, so each one fits into the next like a ball and socket.

pangaea.definition: The supercontinent that joined nearly all of Earth's land when the first dinosaurs lived, before it split into Laurasia and Gondwana.

paraphyletic.definition: Describes a group that includes an ancestor but only some of its descendants, such as reptiles without birds.

paratype.definition: A specimen the authors who named a species listed alongside the holotype. Paratypes help show what the species was like, but the name isn't tied to them.

pennaceous.definition: Of feathers: having a central shaft with a flat vane on each side, like a bird's flight feathers, rather than being simple filaments.

pes.definition: The foot. Pedal means "of the foot".

phylogenetic-analysis.definition: A study that works out how animals are related by comparing many of their features, usually with software that finds the family trees that best fit those features.

plesiomorphic.definition: Describes an ancestral feature, inherited from a distant ancestor and shared widely, so it says little about which animals are most closely related.

pollex.definition: The first finger of the hand, equivalent to the human thumb. In many sauropodomorphs it carried a large claw.

polytomy.definition: A point on a family tree where three or more branches split at once, because the analysis couldn't settle the order in which they branched.

postcranial.definition: Of the skeleton behind the skull: everything but the head.

posterior.definition: Toward the back of the animal, the end with the tail. The opposite of anterior.

preoccupied.definition: Of a name: already given to another animal, so it can't be used again. The later animal needs a replacement name.

procoelous.definition: Describes a vertebra whose main body is hollow at the front and rounded at the back, the reverse of opisthocoelous.

proximal.definition: Closer to the body, or to where a limb or bone attaches. The hip end of the thighbone is its proximal end. The opposite of distal.

radiation.definition: A burst of evolution in which one lineage splits into many species that spread into different ways of life.

referred-specimen.definition: A fossil assigned to a species after it was named, because it shares the species' features. The name isn't tied to it, and a later study can move it to another species.

rostral.definition: Toward the tip of the snout.

sacral-vertebra.definition: One of the vertebrae joined to the hip bones. Fused together, they form the sacrum.

sagittal.definition: Running from front to back along the middle of the body, in the plane that divides the left side from the right.

sister-taxon.definition: The closest relative of a group on a family tree: the two share an ancestor that no other group shares.

specific-epithet.definition: The second part of a species' name, such as rex in Tyrannosaurus rex. It names the species only together with its genus.

subfamily.definition: A group of related genera within a family. Subfamily names end in -inae, as in Tyrannosaurinae.

superfamily.definition: A group of related families. Superfamily names end in -oidea, as in Tyrannosauroidea.

synapomorphy.definition: A new feature shared by the members of a group, inherited from their common ancestor, that sets the group apart from others. Synapomorphies are the evidence for a clade.
synapomorphy.etymology: Greek syn, "together", apo, "away from", and morphe, "form".

synonym.definition: One of two or more names given to the same animal. The oldest name usually takes priority as the senior synonym; later names become junior synonyms and fall out of use.

syntype.definition: One of several specimens that together served as the basis for a name, when no single holotype was chosen.

taxon.definition: Any named group of living things, such as a species, a genus or a clade.

transverse.definition: Running across the body from side to side.

transverse-process.definition: A projection that sticks out sideways from a vertebra, where ribs or muscles attach.

type-species.definition: The species a genus name is tied to. A genus is defined by its type species, as a species is defined by its holotype.

type-specimen.definition: A specimen a species' name is formally tied to: the holotype, or a lectotype or neotype chosen later.

valid.definition: Of a name: properly published and the accepted name for its animal, not a synonym or a doubtful name.

ventral.definition: Toward the belly or underside of the animal. The opposite of dorsal.

vertebra.definition: One of the bones of the backbone, which runs from the skull to the tip of the tail.

wildcard-taxon.definition: An animal whose position jumps around a family tree from one analysis to the next, usually because too little of it is known.
